title: The Solution: Parity Bits
teaches: How Hamming codes insert parity bits at power-of-two positions to detect errors.
visual: Four slots appear labeled P1, D1, P2, D2. Data bits '1' and '0' fill D1 and D2. Parity bits P1 and P2 are calculated and filled with '0' and '1' respectively, forming the codeword '0101'.
narration: Hamming codes insert parity bits at positions that are powers of two. These bits check specific subsets of data to ensure integrity.

title: Correction and Recovery
teaches: Flipping the identified bit restores the original message.
visual: The cursor highlights the bit at index 2. It flips from '0' back to '1'. The final string is displayed as '101' with a green checkmark, confirming successful recovery.
narration: By flipping the identified bit, we restore the original data. Hamming codes allow us not just to detect, but to correct single-bit errors automatically.
